This appeal is on getting dissatisfied by the judgment and award dated 10-12-2012, passed by the learned Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dhule in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.535 of 2008 allowing claim petition of the present respondent {2} FA 3128 of 2013 nos.1 to 3 and holding appellant Insurance Company liable to pay compensation jointly and severally.

had set up claim petition for compensation to the tune of Rs.15,00,000/- by invoking Section 166 of The United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Dilip Chindha Patil And Others on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108916035/

sentences.text: Original Respondent no.1/owner of the offending vehicle, did not appear before the Tribunal.
The above claim was resisted by original respondent no.2/Insurance Company by filing written statement at exh.13.

After appreciating oral and documentary evidence, learned Tribunal was pleased to allow the claim petition directing compensation to be paid by original respondent nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally to the tune of Rs.16,36,700/- with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of impugned order till realization of amount.
Feeling aggrieved by the above decision, Insurance Company/original respondent no.2, has come up in appeal by raising various grounds as stated in the appeal memo.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant Insurance Company would point out that, there was breach of terms and conditions of Policy and statutory defence of driver not holding valid and effective licence at {3} FA 3128 of 2013 the time of incident, was taken.

He submitted that considering the manner in which accident took place, learned Tribunal ought to have saddled contributory liability/negligence on the part of deceased for riding the motorcycle in rash, negligent manner with high speed.
For above reasons, he urged this Court to interfere in the impugned judgment and award and modify the same by directing Insurance Company to first pay and then recover.
Learned counsel invited attention of this Court to the particulars and information of permit of Taxi bearing No. MH-18 E-8584.

He specifically invited attention of this Court to clause (5) pertaining to Validity and Permit and pointed out that validity of Taxi was from 30-07-2002 to 29-07-2007 and it was again renewed on 02-05-2008 and its validity was till 01-05-2013.

Further he pointed out that accident in question had taken place on 19-03-2008 and therefore, vehicle had no valid permit at the time of incident and hence, he submits that there is breach of terms of conditions of policy and therefore, appellant Insurance Company would not be liable to pay compensation as very permit of the vehicle had expired.
In support of above contentions, the learned counsel has placed reliance on judgment dated 20-12-2023 passed by this Court in First Appeal No.2885 of 2019.

Learned counsel for respondent nos.1 and 2, and for respondent no.3 (original claimant nos.1 to 3) pointed out that learned trial Court has not considered and granted compensation towards future prospects in spite of deceased working in Army and was in permanent employment.
That, even interest awarded by learned trial Court is from the date of the order rather than from the date of filing of claim petition.
It is further submitted that meager amount is granted under the heads of consortium, funeral expenses and loss of estate.
Therefore, learned counsel urges to modify the impugned award to this extent and grant compensation as per settled law.

sentences.text:
Though served, none appeared for respondent no.4.
6. Heard.
Perused the papers.
It is emerging that original claimants set up above claim by adducing evidence of father of deceased namely Dilip Patil and one witness namely Nilesh Gawali {5} FA 3128 of 2013 (exh.36).
Admittedly, father of deceased was not an eye witness to the accident.
However, on the strength of spot panchanama and FIR, involvement of offending vehicle came to be gauged.

While refusing to grant compensation towards future prospects, learned Tribunal made certain observations in paragraph 18 of the impugned judgment that, though deceased was 26 years of age,
his retirement was not like other general cases i.e. at the age of 58 years, as it has come on record that his service tenure was 17 years and he had already served for 7 years.
Holding so much, learned Tribunal has held that general rule does not apply.
Such observations are incorrect as, out of 17 years service, deceased had only completed 7 years, and service of 10 years had remained in his credit.
His service is almost like that of permanent commissioned.
Therefore, bearing in mind settled legal position and as the deceased was in permanent employment, compensation towards future prospects need to be awarded.

7. It seems that the learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,000/- towards loss of consortium,
Rs.2,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.2,500/- towards loss of estate.

However, as per law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of National Insurance Company Limited (Supra)
and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd.
 {6} FA 3128 of 2013 (Supra), the claimants are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards consortium, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.

Further it seems that the learned Tribunal applied multiplier of 18 which, as per Sarla Verma and Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors., AIR 2009, SC 3104, is for the age group of 15 to 25 years.

Therefore, Addition of 10% increase for a span of every three years is only on 1,15,000 i.e. 10% of 1,15,000 = 11,500 x 4 = Rs.46,000 B)

However, as pointed out by the learned counsel for the appellant Insurance Company, the offending vehicle i.e. Taxi bearing No. MH-18 E-8584 standing in the name of Vaibhav Narayan Suryawanshi had valid permit only up to 29-07-2007 and thereafter,
it was renewed on 02-05-2008.
As rightly pointed out, accident in present case had taken place on 19-03-2008 and as such offending vehicle was not having valid permit at the time of accident.
Therefore, appellant Insurance Company ought not to have made liable.
Therefore, pay and recover order is required to be passed.

Hence, following order :
ORDER I. Impugned judgment and award dated 10-12-2012 passed by MACT, Dhule in MACP No. 535/2008 stands modified.

II. The original claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.8,64,500/-
along with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization of the amount.
III. It is held that Appellant Insurance Company could not be held liable to pay the compensation and the same is exonerated from the liability.
However, it shall first pay compensation to original claimants and then is entitled to recover the same from original respondent no.1 as per law.
{8} FA 3128 of 2013 IV. Appellant Insurance Company to deposit the amount of enhanced compensation along with interest thereon in this Court.
V. On deposit of amount by the Insurance Company, original claimants are permitted to withdraw the same along with interest, if any.
VI. Modified award be prepared accordingly.
VII. Claimants to pay court fees on enhanced compensation as per Rules.
VIII. The Appeal is disposed of in above terms.
